transcript.content: Hello, how are you doing today? What brings you in to see me?

Hi… I’m doing okay, thanks. I guess what finally pushed me to come in is I keep making these small mistakes in things I turn in—applications, research notes, stuff like that. It’s not huge, exactly, but it’s embarrassing, like I’ll put the wrong date on an artwork label or somehow skip a question, even though I really thought I’d checked it. I’m not sure if that’s the kind of thing worth coming in for, but it’s been happening enough that I thought I should ask.
Have you noticed these kinds of mistakes happening throughout your life, like when you were in school, or is this something that’s mostly started recently?

I think it’s been there for a long time, honestly. Not in a dramatic way, but even in elementary school teachers would write things like, you know, I had good ideas, but I’d forget to turn in worksheets or lose the instructions. Or I’d miss some little detail unless my parents checked my backpack every night. I don’t know if that counts, but it wasn’t only recent.
Can you tell me more about how you organize your daily tasks and whether you often find it hard to stay focused on things you're working on?

Yeah… I mean, I try to be organized. I make lists and I have folders and stuff, so it’s not like I’m not trying. But if I’m being honest, my apartment and my laptop both kind of end up looking like a bunch of half-started projects. Like rent papers mixed in with gallery notes, article PDFs, different to-do lists… and then I’m not always sure what actually needs to happen first.

I can usually get going eventually, but staying focused on one thing without drifting into another task or another tab is harder than I’d like. I don’t know if that’s the kind of thing you mean.
Have you been feeling down, losing interest in things, or struggling with low energy that might be affecting your ability to focus or finish tasks?

Um… I don’t think so? I mean, I have normal bad days, I guess, or I get frustrated with myself when I mess something up. But I wouldn’t say I’ve been really down or that I’ve lost interest in things.

Low energy… maybe sometimes, but not in a way that feels like the main issue. I still want to do the things I care about; it’s more like I don’t always manage them the way I mean to. Does that answer it okay?
Have you ever had periods where you felt unusually energetic, needed less sleep, or felt like your thoughts were racing faster than usual?

I don’t think so, no. I mean, I’ve had nights where I stayed up too late because I got caught up in something, but not like I suddenly didn’t need sleep or felt unusually energized in a big way.

And racing thoughts… maybe when I’m stressed or trying to juggle things, but I don’t think it’s like what you’re asking about. I’m not totally sure where the line is, though. Does that make sense?

Can you describe a time when you had to sit still or focus on something for a while? Did you find it hard to stay in one place, or did you feel like you needed to be doing something else all the time?

I don’t think I’m someone who has to get up and move all the time, if that’s what you mean. Like in a lecture or if I’m watching something, I can stay in the seat.

I might shift around or check the time, or kind of feel like I should be doing something else, but I’m not usually pacing or unable to sit there. It’s more… my attention wanders than my body, I guess. I hope that distinction makes sense.
Have you ever felt so restless or wired that it was hard to relax, even when you wanted to?

Not really, I don’t think. I mean, I get kind of mentally wound up sometimes, like if I have something I’m supposed to do, but I wouldn’t say I feel wired or like I can’t relax at all.

Usually if I want to relax, I can eventually… maybe I just get distracted or feel a little guilty, but not restless in a big physical way. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have you noticed yourself getting more irritable or emotional than usual, especially when things don’t go as planned?

I don’t think so, not more than usual. I mean, I can get a little frustrated if plans change or something doesn’t work out, but I think that’s pretty normal?

I wouldn’t say I’m getting especially emotional or snapping at people. At least, I haven’t noticed that. Does that answer it okay?

Can you describe how you manage tasks that require sustained mental effort, like reading a lengthy document or completing a detailed form? Do you find it especially hard to stay focused on those kinds of tasks?

Yeah… those are probably the tasks I’m worst about, honestly. I don’t mean to avoid them exactly, but if I know something is going to take real concentration, like drafting a curatorial proposal or reading a dense theory chapter, I’ll suddenly decide I should do smaller things first.

Like, I’ll answer emails, tidy up, run an errand—stuff that feels useful—until the bigger task is still sitting there. And then it’s suddenly the night before it’s due and I’m trying to do it all at once.

It’s not that I can’t do it at all, but getting myself to stay with it early enough is hard. Does that make sense?
Have these difficulties with focus and task completion ever significantly impacted your performance at work, school, or in relationships?

Yeah… I mean, I wouldn’t say it’s ruined anything, but it has affected things more than I’d like to admit.

I’ve turned in work late a few times, and I’ve missed a couple of application deadlines because I kept putting off the longer parts until it was basically too late. And one of my mentors did say something like my follow-through was starting to hurt opportunities I should probably be ready for.

That was kind of hard to hear. I know it sounds like just being disorganized, but I’m not trying to blow things off. Does that make sense?
